description: Explanations for every file in the SQLite ratchet register (async SQLite migration plan, DB6). Each remaining synchronous database access on an application thread must match a rule that names its domain, how it is reached, and where it is migrated. `node scripts/qa/sqlite-audit.mjs` fails on a register entry no rule explains.

rules.access: The daemon keeps its synchronous task, workspace, approval and team stores. Its task SQL is WAL reads, which do not wait on writers; the lock stalls came from milestone commits, which run in the worker (slice C2). New responsibility and graph checks use worker-backed units. The control-authority cancellation path retains one synchronous target check inside the immediate task-cancel transaction.
rules.plan: reviewed exception (DB6): stays

rules.access: Protected credential requests and the vault. The vault is encrypted with the keychain on the host and committed with the request row in one IMMEDIATE host transaction (DB5 updateWithin), so a credential lands only while its request is pending. Moving it needs a combined settings-and-request worker command like Pulse's. The operations are rare and user-initiated.
rules.plan: reviewed exception (DB6); DB7 candidate: combined vault commit command

rules.access: Repositories. Slice A (25 leaf repositories: approvals, artifacts, annotations, input requests, permission rules, messaging queues, delivery, rate limits, audit log, curated memory, memory settings and pending writes, worktrees, comparisons, composer drafts, task labels, device profiles and others) and slice B (channels, channel users and sessions, memories, memory embeddings) are now synchronous XStore classes run as storage-domain units behind async XRepository facades (COWORK_DB_WORKER_STORAGE); the stores stay here because session services in the worker use them directly. Channel config is sealed: the host facade encrypts and decrypts it with secure storage and the units store the ciphertext. A few host reads stay synchronous on the stores: the tool catalog and mailbox availability checks, managed-agent Slack target sync (an encrypted-config read-modify-write), and tool descriptions. The work-session repositories stay synchronous stores shared by the session services on the host and in the worker; host-only readers use their read units. Slice C1 moved tasks and workspaces the same way (`TaskStore`, `WorkspaceStore`): deleting a task through the facade first commits the host timeline writer's pending rows for it. The daemon hot path, runtime wiring in `main.ts`, the subconscious loop's workspace paths, host transactions, timeline transports and the session services keep the stores for now. Task events stay a synchronous host repository: timeline writes go through the worker writer when enabled, and reads merge its pending rows instead of writing.
rules.plan: stays: the daemon hot path keeps the stores (reads do not wait on write locks; milestone commits are in the worker since slice C2); the host backend is the rollback path

rules.plan: reviewed exception (DB6); DB7 candidate: async settings managers
